minutes.headline: Assessors reviewed the senior tax-relief presentation slide by slide, set up a subcommittee for the new senior means-tested exemption, and chose to do neighborhood site-index review in house.
minutes.summary: The Board of Assessors heard the principal assessor's monthly report (abatements, deeds, FY26 budget request), then spent most of the meeting editing a public presentation on senior tax exemptions and deferrals for a senior center event. They agreed to a subcommittee on the new senior means-tested exemption, to do neighborhood and site-index review in house, and to draft a placeholder warrant article. No formal votes were audible except the end-of-meeting motion to adjourn.

budget_items.what_was_said: The principal assessor described the lines she submitted to the interim town manager, including salaries, contracted services, maps, postage, supplies, mileage and dues. Several vendor costs rose and no response had come back yet.

budget_items.topic: Cyclical inspections contract with Vision Appraisal
budget_items.what_was_said: A figure was budgeted for cyclical inspections over three years, under a contract the town manager signed with Vision. The Department of Revenue requires a share of properties to be inspected each year.

budget_items.topic: Neighborhood and site-index revision for lake properties
budget_items.what_was_said: An estimate was budgeted for the revision, and the DOR has directed the site indexes to be reviewed. The figures were stated confusingly.
The mapping update line went up and was underfunded, and the personal property vendor's fee also rose.
The board noted last year's overlay budget, that more was spent than budgeted, and that a small amount was transferred out. The members agreed to prepare for an overlay discussion on February 5th.
One residential case is pending and three earlier cases were settled. The members said a residential case would not be a large amount.

budget_items.what_was_said: The assessor cited what a homeowner pays to record a corrected deed and to have one drawn up.

budget_items.topic: Overlay and funding of the senior means-tested exemption
budget_items.what_was_said: Members said the cost of the new senior tax relief would probably come from the overlay and might require raising it. They said the question should be checked with town counsel and discussed on February 5th.

budget_items.topic: Cost-of-living adjustment to exemption income and asset limits
budget_items.what_was_said: The board discussed raising exemption qualification amounts as if the COLA had been adopted earlier. It said the effect on the overlay would be small.

transfers.description: Money transferred out of the assessors' overlay last year, as recalled by members

decisions.decision: The assessors will draft a letter for homeowners who file unclear or multi-parcel deeds, asking them to go back to their attorney. The principal assessor will also contact the registry of deeds, and the letter will be reviewed by the board.
The members agreed to finish the backlog of minutes edits for the February 5th meeting and to send changes a few days ahead.
The members agreed to add the HERO Act as a fifth bullet to the exemptions slide, and to name the veterans' representative.
The members agreed to pull the senior circuit breaker pages, roughly 13 through 18, out of the presentation. They may be used as a handout or a tax professional may be invited before April 15.
A note will be added near the front of the 41A deferral section that a mortgage or lien holder must approve entry into the program.

A subcommittee will work out the process for the Lunenburg senior tax relief law. It would include the principal assessor and a board member plus Lou and Tom, with a target of two months or less. The principal assessor will seek a flowchart from the Westford assessor.
The members agreed to do the neighborhood and site-index review in house, starting with the lake properties but looking at the whole town. Nothing will be implemented until the review is done.
The assessors' old-versus-new parcel spreadsheet with land use codes and site index will be posted to the assessor website.
The principal assessor will draft a placeholder warrant article on updating the exemption income and asset limits for the next meeting.
The chair asked that the presentation slides not name a board member as 'Jane's husband', and that 'select persons' be corrected to 'select board'. The board member agreed to fix both.

what_happened.line: The Board of Assessors agreed to set up a subcommittee to work out the process for the new senior means-tested tax exemption, with a target of two months or less.
Members agreed to review neighborhood and site-index values in house, starting with the lake properties, and to implement nothing until the review is done.
Most of the meeting went to editing a public presentation on senior exemptions and deferrals; the senior circuit breaker pages were pulled out and a HERO Act bullet added.
Members said the new senior exemption would probably be paid for from the overlay, possibly raising it, and deferred that question to February 5th.
The principal assessor will draft a placeholder warrant article on exemption income and asset limits for the next meeting. No formal votes were audible.

why_it_matters: A new senior means-tested exemption is likely to be paid for from the overlay, the reserve for abatements and exemptions, so the cost could be spread across other taxpayers' bills rather than appearing as a separate line.
A review of site-index values for lake properties could change how those homes are assessed, though the board said nothing will take effect until the review is finished.
Updated exemption income and asset limits would likely need a warrant article, which is a vote residents may be asked to take at town meeting.
watch_next: February 5th meeting: overlay discussion, the draft placeholder warrant article on exemption limits, and a check with town counsel on funding the senior exemption.
The subcommittee's process for the senior means-tested exemption, targeted for two months or less.
